To make the world us. Only ours to shape.|sound=Hank MacLean.ogg}} '''Henry "Hank" MacLean''' is a prominent character {{in|FOTV}}. He is the father of [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[Norm MacLean]] and husband of [[Rose MacLean]] and stood as [[overseer]] of [[Vault 33]] until [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], when his abduction from the Vault by the forces of [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] leads to Lucy's mission to brave the wasteland in order to rescue him. ==Background== ===Origins=== Hank was born sometime before the [[Great War]] and later entered a career with the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] as [[Barb Howard]]'s executive assistant. He was a fan of his boss' husband [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]'s film work in [[Hollywood]] and always desired to meet him and get his autograph. According to Cooper during a later confrontation, one of Hank's duties as Barb's assistant was picking up her dry cleaning. After meeting [[Steph Harper]], they got married in Las Vegas. Hank got her into [[Bud Askins]]' [[Bud's Buds|program]].{{FOTV|2|8}} At some point, Hank secretly became an agent of the [[Enclave]]. Hank secretly kept an Enclave [[Pip-Boy]] in a keepsake box to communicate with them. Steph was aware of his ties to and work for the Enclave. Hank entered [[Cryonics|cryonic]] sleep on the eve of the Great War as one of "[[Bud's Buds]]," a group of Vault-Tec employees chosen by Vault-Tec senior junior vice president [[Bud Askins]] to be preserved within [[Vault 31]] of the [[Three Vaults]] underneath [[Santa Monica]], where he slept for over a century. He was released from cryonic sleep on August 9, 2268 to integrate into the current generation of Vault dwellers, being assigned to [[Vault 33]]. After time spent there, Hank was elected the overseer in 2271 and served in that role up until 2296.[[Fallout (TV series)]] Episode 5: "[[The Past]]" [[File:Rose MacLean.png|thumb|250px|Hank's wife – Rose MacLean]] As part of the Three Vaults' true purpose under Bud's Buds, wherein Vaults 32 and 33's populations were to be breeding pools by the pre-War inhabitants of Vault 31 to create a race of "super managers," Hank met a woman, [[Rose MacLean|Rose]], who was born in a Vault and never saw the surface. The two of them were married and started a family, with two children: a daughter, [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]], and a son, [[Norm MacLean|Norman]]. This was in spite of the fact that Hank was still married to Steph who wouldn't be released from cryonic sleep until a number of years after him. ===Going to the surface=== Sometime around [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2277|2277]], Rose deduced that Vault 33's water supply was being siphoned off by someone from outside, on the surface, which she took as proof that civilization had re-emerged. However, when she confided this to her husband, Hank pointedly dismissed her questioning and forbade her from trying to investigate, which caused Rose to become suspicious of him. Eventually, her doubts about Hank grew too big to ignore. One day, Rose took her two children and escaped Vault 33 to the surface, angering Hank because he viewed this as endangering their children, both in terms of a physical riskHank MacLean: ''"Lucy? I loved your mother. But she stopped being your mother when she left home. When she took you into danger. You've seen what it's like up here. Everyone equally afraid, equally miserable. Forced to do horrible things in order to survive. Lucy... I had to make a choice. Between their violent world and our peaceful one. And I believe, Lucy, I know I made the right choice."''
({{FOTV|1|8}}) but also an ideological one, as he feared they would be influenced by the violence and survival instincts instilled by life in the wasteland, which would ruin Vault-Tec's mission for their Vault.Hank MacLean: ''"We never got to discuss All Quiet, did we? I guess we were waiting 'til after the wedding. Right? That end, that was a humdinger, huh?"''
[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"I didn't finish it."''
Hank: ''"That's okay. You've been busy. What did you think about the parts that you did read?"''
Lucy: ''"I found it very upsetting."''
Hank: ''"Can't disagree with you there. What aspect upset you most?"''
Lucy: ''"[scoffs]"''
Hank: ''"To me, the most troubling was that everyone seemed to be fighting over nothing. The French and the German, what was the difference between them, really? I mean, other than the uniforms? I saw the same thing up on the surface. People fighting over the most petty things, like bottle caps. Is that what you saw when you were there? But, you know, some things just never change. People just wanna kill each other, don't they? I think it's the only way for people to feel safe. It's ironic. To feel safe, we have to hurt people. Even kill them, because the-- [...] It's crazy... the war instinct, hm?"''
Lucy: ''"I'm bringing you back to Vault 33 to face justice. For murdering the citizens of Shady Sands. You have the right to remain silent until the Vault Council assigns you a legal counselor."''
Hank: ''"For a second there, I thought the Wasteland had changed you."''
[...]
Lucy: ''"What are you doing?"''
Hank: ''"Surrendering."''
Hank: ''"I did what I did to protect you. But maybe it came at too high a price. And there comes a time in a man's life when he has to take responsibility for what he's done, and for me, that time has come. You have come, Sugarbomb."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) Apparently with [[Betty Pearson]] in tow, Hank himself left the Vault to chase after her, eventually tracking his family down to [[Shady Sands]], the capital city of the [[New California Republic]]. The exact circumstance of their confrontation are unclear, but it ended with Rose refusing to return to the Vault while Hank was able to return with both of his children. However, his discovery of the NCR and its attempt to restore civilization spurred Hank to make another trip to the surface in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2283|2283]] where he used a [[brain-computer interface chip]] to mind-control an [[NCR caravaner]] into carting an armed [[Nuclear weapons|nuclear device]] into the heart of the city in an attempt to wipe out the post-War nation. He came to believe that this was done to erase the blight of factionalism and warfare in the wasteland, and to ensure the world could be remade according to Vault-Tec's ideals. While he made sure that his children were spared, Hank decidedly left Rose behind, and she eventually degenerated into a [[ghoul]], presumably due to the radiation left behind by the blast.{{FOTV|1|8}} To cover this up, Hank told his children as they grew up that their mother perished during the "Plague of '77" and that his grief caused him to drop to an unhealthy 128 pounds. Lucy further insists, when telling this to [[the Ghoul]], that Hank and the rest of Vault 33 would rather starve than resort to [[cannibalism]]; the Ghoul expresses his skepticism about this.{{FOTV|1|4}} She also believed that her father would be heartbroken to find out that his daughter was responsible for destroying an independent society while convincing [[Maximus]] to return [[Vault 4]]'s [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]].{{FOTV|1|6}} ===Vault Overseer=== [[File:Lucy and Hank experimenting.webp|thumb|250px|Lucy and Hank doing a science project]] After safely returning to Vault 33 with nobody the wiser, Hank resumed his duties as overseer and continued raising his two children. In this capacity, Hank's scientific skills and people skills contributed to his role as an effective leader, to the degree that he became the "glue" that held the Vault 33 community together. Private time with his family was spent watching movies or gardening with his daughter, or engaging in family book club discussions with both Lucy and Norm. He ensured they were raised with little to no knowledge about the outside world except for what was found in select books (like ''[[War and Peace]]'' and ''[[All Quiet on the Western Front]]'') and films or what he chose to teach to them.{{FOTV|1|1}} {{clear}} ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A kind and loving father to Lucy and Norm and benevolent Overseer to Vault 33, Hank is the glue that binds their small underground community together. He has a knack for science and exceptional people skills. He believes it is the shared duty of every Vault dweller to keep the candle of civilization lit.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 10.jpg|thumb|250px|Hank speaking at Lucy's wedding]] In 2296, Hank organizes a trade with [[Vault 32]] of supplies for a breeder named [[Monty (TV series)|Monty]] to marry his daughter Lucy. He personally welcomes the Vault 32 dwellers, including their overseer [[Lee Moldaver]], who informed him of the passing of previous overseer [[Ian Jackson]]. Later, at the wedding ceremony, Hank gives a speech blessing Lucy and Monty and mentions their children will likely be able to reclaim the surface. [[File:FOTV Trailer 1 47.png|thumb|250px|left|Hank speaking to Lucy before he is abducted]] The Vault 32 residents reveal themselves to be a [[Vault 32 raider|group of raiders]] and attack [[Vault 33]]'s residents. During the fight, Hank saves Lucy and drowns Monty to death. Hank and Lucy then find several Vault 33 dwellers held hostage. He said he thought he knew who Moldaver was, and she replied everyone knew who she was. Moldaver offers Hank a vague choice between Lucy and the vault dwellers, although it is unclear if she means to be killed or held prisoner. Hank chooses to shove Lucy into a room, telling her she means "the world" to him. Hank is then tranquilized by the raiders and kidnapped from Vault 33. ====[[The Beginning]]==== [[File:Hank caged.png|thumb|250px|Hank caged by Moldaver]] Lucy enters the [[Griffith Observatory]] and finds her father trapped in a giant cage. However, Moldaver begins exposing Hank's atrocities, and Hank desperately tries to convince Lucy that she is lying. This does not work for Lucy, who believes Moldaver and becomes visibly upset. Lucy demands her father give Moldaver the code to [[cold fusion]], which he reluctantly does, and Moldaver activates it. However, the Brotherhood of Steel arrives to attack, and Moldaver leaves to defend the base of the [[New California Republic]]. [[File:Hank in Mojave.png|thumb|left|250px|Hank escaping in power armor]] The Brotherhood gained the upper hand, and Hank was released from his cage by [[Maximus]], but Lucy revealed to Maximus that her father was responsible for the bombing of Shady Sands. Infuriated, Maximus attacked Hank but was knocked out by him, as Hank had already entered a suit of [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] he had removed from a headless knight's body. Lucy then held her father at gunpoint, but he did not believe she would shoot him. The Ghoul entered and shot at Hank, asking Hank where his family was. Hank did not reply, instead choosing to turn and flee using the T-60 armor's jets to propel himself away from the observatory. Lucy and the Ghoul decided to go after him in order to find out where he was going and the answers they believed would be found there with him. Sometime later, Hank had traversed far into the [[Mojave Wasteland]], stopping on a ridge overlooking the distant city of [[New Vegas]]. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Hank is the beloved Overseer of Vault 33 and Lucy and Norm’s proud father. He is dedicated to changing the world for the ‘better’ (as defined by his specific ideals) and will stop at nothing in pursuit of that goal, no matter how narrow-minded or self-serving it may be.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} At some point after leaving [[New California]], Hank made a detour from his route to New Vegas to go to [[Vault 24]]. Along the way, he brutally killed one wastelander by stomping on his abdomen, crushing it, then kidnapped [[Sunburned man|the son]] of [[Old Woman Gretch]] shortly after and brought him along. Inside Vault 24, Hank obtained the hard drive containing the Vault staff's research into enhancing the [[brain-computer interface chip]], then attached one to his captive and left him behind to serve as a messenger for his pursuers, knowing they would be able to follow him that far. ====[[The Innovator]]==== [[File:FTV S2E1 Still 253.png|thumb|250px|Hank dressing for the occasion]] Hank's long trek eventually ends at the entrance to an [[Las Vegas management Vault|underground facility]] emblazoned with Vault-Tec symbols, of which he relished the sight. He enters and finds his way to a computer room, reactivating one of the [[terminal]]s to test that he still has access to Vault-Tec's computer systems. Once he confirms this, he first makes an effort to pour a fresh pot of coffee and take a sip. Afterward, he exits the armor in order to clean up, tend to his facial wound left by the Ghoul, and pick out a set of proper work attire, including a gold-plated Pip-Boy. With that, Hank explores the rest of the facility and finds his way into the "Global Comms" room, where he works the ham radio console to find the right frequency. Through the microphone, he speaks to an unspecified recipient he calls "sir," revealing that he is in Las Vegas, beneath the notice of anyone left from Vault-Tec. He describes the city as the recipient's "old stomping grounds" and voices his belief that the recipient would have found a way to stay alive this long owing to a knack for "calculations." As his conversation is narrated, it's shown that his further exploration turned up evidence that the facility staff were performing experiments to miniaturize the black box chip and make it almost undetectable, which he says he intends to combine with the results of Vault 24's work to perfect it. He ends his call by boasting that his work there will prove his value and that the recipient will "be begging [him] to help." {{clear}} ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== In a flashback to 2283, the events of Hank's plan to destroy Shady Sands are shown in full. Shortly after getting the confirmation of the detonation via his Pip-Boy, Hank washes his hands in the bathroom of his home in Vault 33, looking at himself in the mirror in contemplation of his actions, before being drawn to his daughter asking him to read her a story. In the present, the early stages of Hank's experiments to perfect the black box chip lead him to seek out the facility's cryonic biorepository, where a supply of experimental mice are kept in stasis. However, he repeatedly runs into failure when trying to test the upper limits of the chip's signal as it proves too strong and violently explodes his test subjects without producing meaningful results. A later trip through the facility finds him outside the "Premium Elite Plus" section, which triggers an idea. Even later, Hank is revealed to have thawed [[Stephen Winthrop]], a pre-War customer of Vault-Tec who purchased a ticket to be cryonically preserved in the PEP section, and implanted him with a black box. Steve wonders if he was brought out because of [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]]; Hank claims that it is, but not as Vault-Tec planned. As Hank prepares the chip signal for his current experiment, he remarks about his preference for "the classics" and how much has changed in the world. Steve becomes more aware of his helpless state as Hank reveals that Steve did not include his family in the program, which he claims was because it was too expensive to buy more than one ticket. Hank emphasizes how a commitment to family builds a civilization, then compares it to his experiments, claiming that through enhancing the black box, he will also improve a piece of "outdated technology" — civilization. Steve begins to react to the black box's signal as Hank increases its strength, eventually resulting in Steve's explosive death; Hank coldly remarks "if at first you don't succeed... try, try again." ====[[The Wrangler]]==== In a pre-War flashback, the younger Hank meets up with Barb and Cooper at [[Los Angeles International Airport]] for their trip to the corporate conference in Las Vegas. When Hank offers to take their bags, Cooper points out the briefcase handcuffed to his wrist, which Hank says makes him like both a V.I.P. and a potential assassination target before Barb sends him ahead. After coming back from a private meeting with [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]], Cooper sees Hank conversating with his fellow junior managers [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]] and [[Pete (TV series)|Pete]]. After reaching the city and going to the conference's venue at the [[Lucky 38]], Hank mingles with partygoers and goes to an upstairs bar to have some drinks. He is followed by Cooper, who is trying to get at his briefcase, thinking it contains the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]]; before Cooper can act on his plan, he is drawn away to a meeting with [[Robert House]]. In the present, after the results of his experiment with Steve achieving a new baseline with the chip, Hank continues with human testing. He leaves the facility and eventually locates the [[snake oil salesman]] at an [[abandoned taco stand]] on a date with [[Fisto]]. When the salesman notices him, he mistakes Hank for a "looky-loo" and tells him to watch from behind a shrub, like a "civilized pervert;" before he can resume his date, Hank bludgeons him with a crowbar and takes him back to the facility. The salesman later awakens in Hank's workstation, where Hank asks him if he would like to forget all his memories while retaining his language and motor skills. The snake oil salesman answers "Please. Yes." which delights Hank as he begins to turn up the signal's strength. At first, the salesman seems pleased and even aroused, but then begins to wince seemingly in pain and screaming, almost repeating Steve's final fate until the chip achieves the necessary threshold, turning the salesman into a mindless slave and proving Hank's work to be a success. Relishing the results, Hank remarks that "it's time to begin" and presses a button on his console to start the next stage of his plan. Sometime later, Hank discovered that the facility contained a cryonic suspension wing for management and that among its occupants were his former boss Barb and her daughter [[Janey Howard|Janey]]. Once he later discovered that Lucy and the Ghoul had ignored his previous warning to stop following him and were active in New Vegas, he devised a plan and sent the salesman (cleaned and dressed up as a proper Vault-Tec worker) as his representative. Through him, Hank relayed to them that he had found Cooper's family and was willing to make a deal: the bounty hunter would return Lucy to the safety of [[Vault 33]] while Hank finalized his plans, and no harm would come to the Howards; simultaneously, he threatened to prematurely end their stasis and kill them if his demands were not met. The Ghoul ultimately complies with Hank's order and [[Tranq gun (TV series)|tranquilizes]] Lucy, which the salesman takes as acceptance and leaves them to relay the new to Hank. However, shortly after this, Lucy manages to power through the tranquilizer and use her [[Power fist (TV series)|power fist]] to punch the Ghoul through the window of their hotel room in the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]], leaving him impaled on a pole on the streets of [[Freeside]], then collapsing from the full effects immediately. Apparently having anticipated this turn of events, Hank shows up in person to collect Lucy, greeting her by using her nickname "Sugarbomb" as she fully falls unconscious. ====[[The Other Player]]==== In another pre-War flashback, during a workday at the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] in Los Angeles, Hank convinces [[Betty Pearson]] to let him substitute in her place during Barb's meeting with [[Robert House's double|Robert House]] (in truth his body double). He observes with keen interest as the [[RobCo Industries]] CEO shows off the "automated man" technology he developed, the black box chip, and how he will trade it to Vault-Tec in exchange for getting ownership of the cold fusion diode. Later in the pre-War timeline, after Cooper confronts Barb with his knowledge of Vault-Tec's plans and learns about her own circumstances, Cooper returns to the casino floor of the Lucky 38 and finds Hank still drinking at the bar; he gets involved and manages to get Hank more drunk. He later walks the utterly hammered assistant back to the hotel room and secretly drugs him with sleeping pills in order to access the briefcase. However, he only finds an injector gun, and once Barb returns, she uses it to extract the cold fusion diode from within Hank's neck, a security measure that clues Cooper in to how well-prepared Barb was to protect it. In the present, after returning to the facility and placing the unconscious Lucy in a furnished observation room to let her sleep, Hank arranged for her to receive a yellow dress and left instructions for her to call him once she woke up. When she eventually does, however, Lucy's suspicions and doubts about her father after learning about his past crimes lead her to shirk the gift and go look for him. This leads her to discover that the facility had now becoming a functioning assembly line with numerous [[X-Branch office worker|office workers]] that Hank had systematically abducted and brainwashed with the chips, ranging from rival tribesmen to murderers to members of [[Caesar's Legion]], with many working to produce more chips for further use. Lucy eventually finds her way to a room marked "Simulation" where the interior is designed to look almost exactly like the resident quarters of her home Vault. She notices Hank as he is in the middle of setting out a meal on the table. He tries to break the silence by pointing out that they never got to finish their book club reading of ''[[All Quiet on the Western Front]]'' that he had planned for the day after her wedding. Lucy admits that she never finished it, but when Hank asks about what she did read, she says she found it upsetting. Hank remarks on what he saw as the troubling nature of the book, how both sides fought over seemingly nothing, and compares it to the present state of the wasteland where people still fight over "nonsensical" things like [[bottle cap]]s. As Hank turns the topic to mankind and their [[Themes in the Fallout series|instinct for war]], Lucy ambushes him from behind, using a pair of scissors she swiped from the office as a weapon, startling him. Lucy reveals that her oft-mentioned goal to bring Hank to justice requires taking him back to Vault 33 to face trial before the Vault council for his crimes, including the destruction of [[Shady Sands]]. Unperturbed, Hank commends Lucy for, in his eyes, not letting the wasteland change who she was at heart. He acquiesces to her demand and even handcuffs himself to show that he is surrendering to her. Lucy remains unconvinced while Hank tells her that everything he did was in the name of protecting her, but now claims that he admits he has to face the consequences of what he did. Before that, however, he tries to emphasize the value of what he sees as "redemptive" progress with the black box technology while Lucy decries it as brainwashing. As she starts to march her father to the door, he switches to bringing up a past memory of a childhood science experiment Lucy did in order to minimize his experiments as a "little project." Though conflicted, Lucy nonetheless sticks to keeping Hank moving as they look for an exit. Lucy tries to escort Hank through the facility discreetly, but as they go back through the assembly room, they are spotted by [[Shelley (TV series)|Shelley]], alerting all of the office workers to the situation. Hank reassures everyone and tells them that Lucy is pursuing justice, which calms them. Lucy questions where he found all of them and Hank reveals that he gathered his "staff" from all over, introducing a few members, including the "kind-of" murderer [[Marjorie (TV series)|Marjorie]] who sharpens pencils; [[Gregory (TV series)|Gregory]] and [[Sherman (TV series)|Sherman]], who were former tribal enemies willing to kill each other; and [[Rita (TV series)|Rita]], who supposedly "cooked people" for Caesar's Legion and now makes trail mix. Hank then approaches a closed door to press a button, revealing it as an express elevator back to the surface (a "management perk," as he calls it). Lucy tries to tell the workers that they are all free to leave and return to the surface too, but they respond that they like living in the safety of the facility more. Once he sees Lucy's confusion, Hank offers that they can stay as long as they like, but after he and Lucy go, they will leave the doors open for them to leave if they wish. At that moment, the snake oil salesman and another worker wheel in the captured [[Biff (TV series)|Ranger Biff]] and a [[Massive legionary|legionary]] bound to chairs, asking what to do with them. Hank reveals to Lucy that he has managed to automate the brainwashing process to the point of simply needing to press a big red button on a nearby console to activate the chips, but Lucy refuses to do it, which Hank seemingly agrees with. Lucy also orders for them to free the two men. However, the legionary breaks free and immediately begins attacking Biff. Lucy attempts to help Biff while Hank merely watches, telling her it is an example of the violence that he is trying to prevent via the chips, even when the legionary directly attacks Lucy. Soon, the legionary starts to repeatedly bludgeon Biff with a stapler, and Hank advises Lucy to press the button and stop the fight, which she does so reluctantly to save Biff. The brainwashing takes effect just before the legionary can land another hit, and his violent demeanor turns to a cheerful, friendly one as he and Biff help each other out to go get cleaned up. Seeing the results, Lucy is left glaring at Hank, realizing that he orchestrated this whole scenario to try and convince her that he is right; Hank smirks and remarks to his daughter "Kum ba yah." ====[[The Handoff]]==== Inside the Las Vegas management Vault, Lucy watches the office workers continue making the chips, which she remarks is one way to save the world but still "wrong;" Hank counters that "perfect" is the enemy of "good," indicating he sees the brainwashing and loss of identity as necessary to restore the surface. Lucy asks Hank what the chip does to the victims' brains, and Hank tells her that the strength of the signal the chip puts out determines how effective the amnesia and loss of memory is, followed by the work of the "mainframe" to implant new thoughts that turn them into "good" people. Lucy maintains her stance to end the brainwashing, but Hank clarifies that the memory loss is irreversible. She instead asks for a way to stop him from making more, which he offers freely by telling her that she must destroy the mainframe providing the chips' programming, located in the basement some distance away. He then gets the idea to have Lucy learn how to drive a golf cart, even though she does not know what that is; Hank remarks with a smile that they're going to have some fun. Hank takes a passenger seat on the cart while Lucy comically struggles to learn the controls. During the ride, Hank wishes woefully that their family could have had a normal life; Lucy throws it back by saying that they did have one and he ended up wrecking it. They eventually end up at the door into the basement level, where more workers are going about their business. Hank leads her directly to the door into the mainframe room, meanwhile as Lucy begins planning out how to make a bomb and Hank comments on it; he joyfully encourages her to think through all her options. Just as they reach the door, they are called out to by the brainwashed legionary from before, which stops Lucy in her tracks. Hank notices that the sight of the violent legionary now cheerfully mopping the floors has gotten her to reconsider how the chips could be used to pacify serious threats like the Legion, with Hank pushing forward the idea that Lucy can help him do it, which gets her to let go of her plan to destroy the mainframe for the time being. Later on, father and daughter have a meal together just like they did back in Vault 33, with Lucy wearing the dress that Hank had got for her. They initially share pleasant conversation, with Lucy remarking on the taste of the mashed potatoes and Hank saying they were always her favorite. However, Lucy then sees the brainwashed Biff coming to refill their water glasses and is reminded of the real cost of using the chips. She tries to gauge how much Biff remembers of his former life but finds he does not even remember meeting her days ago; Hank tries to get Lucy to stop, to no avail, and has to dismiss Biff himself. As he goes for a pie baking in the oven, Hank admonishes Lucy for trying to work against the chip's programming and reveals his belief that there is no difference between Caesar's Legion and the New California Republic with its taxes, expansionist tendencies, and "unpopular" foreign policy, both being "problematic" instances of surface dwellers that must be pacified. He also claims that Lucy would understand his views when she grew older. As he takes the pie out, he touches the hot pan and burns himself, which seemingly gets Lucy to come over to unlock the handcuffs he is still wearing. As she unlocks the first cuff, she tells her father that she understands that the Legion is an army of murderous slavers and rapists while the NCR is just "vaguely problematic." She then tricks Hank by clamping the open cuff onto the oven handle and steals his Pip-Boy while he is distracted, shocking and angering Hank. Lucy tells him that he was actually a good father to her, as her upbringing helped prevent her from turning into a "fudging idiot," referring to her learning not to trust Hank's manipulative behavior. He shouts after her as she leaves to go destroy the mainframe while he remains trapped. ====[[The Strip]]==== In the Las Vegas management Vault's basement, Lucy destroys the mainframe, which she discovered to be the disembodied but still-living head of [[Diane Welch]], who begs for death in order to stop Hank's plans. In a pre-War flashback at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]], a young Hank meets Cooper and Barb Howard to thank Cooper for introducing him to his new fiancee, Steph Harper; he reveals that after Steph took him back to his hotel room the previous night, they ended up talking late into the night, with Hank being wooed into proposing to Steph at 4 a.m. in the morning. He remarks on how Steph has an unbelievable resume for a maid and suggests that Barb talk to Bud Askins about getting Steph a job with Vault-Tec. It's then that Hank realizes that his parents might just kill him for suddenly getting married, but Steph reassures him as she whisks him away. Back in 2296, Hank has managed to escape from the oven which Lucy handcuffed him to and also discovered that she destroyed the Black Box chips' mainframe. He confronts Lucy as she is distraught about having killed Welch, expressing disappointment at her for doing so. Callously, Hank begins to talk about the Black Box chips, comparing Robert House to a robot and saying that he wanted to improve on House's work by adding "personality" to his product via Welch. Hank then reveals Welch's identity to Lucy after she asks, saying that Welch had the ideal personality type for what he wanted to bring to the wasteland; well-meaning, sweet, and non-threatening. Hank then reveals his end goal to Lucy, presenting a miniaturized Black Box chip, which he says is so small that it can be effectively hidden, with the only sign of a person having one of these chips installed being a small scar on the back of their neck. Just then, the brainwashed legionary who had previously strangled Lucy enters the room, and Hank reveals that he intends to install the miniature chip on Lucy and brainwash her into being his model daughter. Though Lucy resists, she is unable to escape the massive legionary, and Hank prepares to implant the chip into her neck. However, Hank is stopped by the Ghoul, who kills the massive legionary and shoots Hank in the buttock, incapacitating him. He then gives Lucy his [[Knuckle Duster]] and leaves Hank's fate in her hands. Hank remains slumped over, watching Lucy as she internally debates what to do with him. Later, Lucy and Hank exit the Lucky 38 out into the deserted New Vegas Strip, where it is revealed that Hank has a scar on the back of his neck; Lucy had implanted the miniature chip inside him. Hank remarks on the view, and Lucy says that she dreamed of one day getting to visit the outside world with the father she loved; Hank admits that he wanted to make it a place worthy of Lucy's dreams. He tells her that he almost wanted to go back to their home, so he could see familiar faces like Norm, Betty, and particularly Steph, but correctly deduces that they are not going back to the Vault; Lucy remarks that the surface changes a person. Hank emphasizes the coming threat of the Legion and tries to convince Lucy to join him in stopping them. She instead asks him to tell her what he was really doing in Vegas, but he counters by asking what she will do once he does. Lucy admits that she is willing to use the chip to turn him into the father she wished she had instead of the man who lied to her throughout her entire life. Hank taunts Lucy's idea of the future and claims that the wasteland has been the real experiment, not the Vaults, which surprises Lucy. He continues by revealing that he has already sent agents out into the wasteland, implanted with the latest model of miniaturized chips to make them undetectable. He sits down on the casino steps while secretly taking out a second remote, stating that these agents are set to carry out orders that were written for them before the Great War. Lucy tries to get him to explain, but a saddened Hank simply tells her that he loves her, then reveals his remote. Lucy tries to stop him but fails to stop Hank from activating his chip and erasing his own memories, which leaves him sitting on the steps with a blank expression. Despairing, Lucy hugs Hank, and he regains awareness but seemingly no longer recognizes her, innocently asking to wipe away a smudge from her face. Through tears, Lucy stands up and walks away from her father, who returns to his blank expression. The event momentarily leaves Lucy in despair, feeling completely lost, though she is brought out of the state when she reunites with Maximus right afterwards. ==Personality== [[File:Hank hugging Lucy.png|thumb|250px|Hank hugging Lucy before her wedding]] Hank MacLean likes to portray himself as the embodiment of old-world American values, prioritizing family, community, and human decency. However, Hank's greatest loyalty is to the values espoused by Vault-Tec, and he is incredibly dismissive to the value of human life and free will if they inconvenience his own views and those of the company he represents. He is a true believer in the company's mission, and genuinely believes it will bring about a better society.See [[#Behind the scenes|the quotes below]] from [[Kyle MacLachlan]]. However, Hank is also ambitious. He displays an individualistic, self-serving streak in attempting to bring the mission to reality in his own way, which he seems to believe will ingratiate himself with whomever he formerly served and possibly lead to a "promotion." This is illustrated by his decision to head to the [[Las Vegas management Vault]], which seems to be a personal choice on his part rather than plans made by the rest of the company.Hank MacLean: ''"This is Hank MacLean, reporting for duty, sir. Nobody in Vault-Tec knows I'm here. And nobody in Vault-Tec knows much of anything anymore. Wanted to let you know I'm still alive. I hope you are, too. I mean, I don't doubt that you are. You spent so much time... calculating how to survive all possible contingencies. Uh, I've been keeping busy. I'm in Vegas these days, back in your old stomping grounds, actually... trying to pick up where you all left off. Looks like a couple of the Vault experiments ran into some speed bumps. 24 made progress on the brain-computer interface. This one, miniaturization. What it all needs is integrating. But I'm confident that if I just roll up my sleeves, I can bring it all home for you. Then, we can finally talk about my promotion. I'm gonna complete the work you started. And when this is all over, you will be begging me to help you."''
({{FOTV|2|1}}) Betty Pearson, one of Hank's former coworkers in Vault-Tec and in Vault 33, also notes that Hank was known to be secretive.[[Betty Pearson]]: ''"Henry. You and your secrets."''
({{FOTV|2|7}}) This is because Hank was secretly serving the [[Enclave]] and their plans which only his wife [[Steph Harper]] knew about. Because of this, Hank expresses a simplistic view of morality, seeing things as wholly good or evil on the basis of how they align with Vault-Tec's societal values. He considers the NCR and Legion to be equally evil forces in the Wasteland, morally equating the high taxes and expansionism of the NCR with the slavery and crucifixion of the Legion, believing that both factions should be eradicated—and overall, that ''all'' factions apart from Vault-Tec should be eliminated. He believes that factionalism is the heart of human suffering and chaos in the wasteland, comparing the status of the wasteland to an endless turmoil of people killing each for what he considers pointless reasons, analogous to how (as he interprets) [[World War I]] is viewed as a pointless conflict between practically identical nations in the novel ''[[All Quiet on the Western Front]]''. Hank is willing to get his hands dirty and places little value on human life outside of those adhering to Vault-Tec's goals: he personally orchestrated the destruction of Shady Sands, causing mass death. On an individual level, he also has no qualms about causing the deaths of human test subjects, even pre-War Americans, seeing these as merely stepping stones to the greater goal.{{FOTV|2|2}}: Hank's scene with [[Stephen Winthrop]]. He justifies his actions with the belief that he is taking murderers and others who have been locked in conflict and violence on the surface and giving them new lives as happy, polite, and unified workers insulated from the wasteland's horrors.{{FOTV|2|6}} He was even willing to cause his wife's death due to her threatening Vault-Tec's mission when she discovered Shady Sands had survived and refused to let go. Hank does show some slight degree of guilt for his actions, as he is shown to be slightly distraught upon receiving confirmation that Shady Sands had been destroyed under his machinations, and he desperately tried to keep Lucy from discovering his actions when Lee Moldaver revealed them to her. When Lucy finally manages to confront him, he is willing to submit to all her demands, stating that while his actions might have been necessary, they might have come at too high a price. However, this was just an attempt to manipulate Lucy to taking his position, and when she went to destroy his brainwashing mainframe he became angry and frantic, whereas he had previously been calm and accommodating.{{FOTV|2|7}} Though he seems to treasure his children, especially Lucy, Hank's familial love is compromised by his dogmatism, as was the case with his wife, and with Lucy when he repeatedly tried to manipulate her into accepting his ideals and then finally attempted to brainwash her into his desired obedient form. Even after this was foiled and Lucy captured him, Hank remained unrepentant about his overall plans, but acknowledged the pain he had caused his daughter just before he chose to activate his own Black Box chip, seemingly wiping all of his memories. While this was done in part to prevent his secrets from being revealed, it may have also partially been to spare Lucy from having to do it herself, as she had realized that the Black Box chip would be the only way to neutralize her father without killing him.[[Ella Purnell]]: ''"Lucy has realized that [Hank] is too dangerous. He almost black-boxed her that there's no way she's gonna get him back to her vault to face a real trial. So I think she realizes what she wants is to keep him alive, but she just wishes he was the moral person that she grew up thinking he was. And here, she's actually going to use this technology against him. And that conflict that she was feeling about the whole Wasteland is, "Is this the answer to the whole Wasteland? No, it is maybe though the solution to my father." "''
